;; problogex_advars_smokers.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type sym (c_1) (c_2) (c_3) (c_4))
(define-type tuple1 (T1 a1))
(define-type tuple2 (T2 a1 a2))
(define (eq_person a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_friend a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_stress a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_influences a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_smokes a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_asthma a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))

;; person/1: 4 facts
(define person_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_3)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_4)) (Sure))
  (Nil))))))
;; friend/2: 5 facts
(define friend_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_1) (c_2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_2) (c_1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_2) (c_4)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_3) (c_2)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_4) (c_2)) (Sure))
  (Nil)))))))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((person_base (draw_all person_facts))
        (friend_base (draw_all friend_facts))
        (friend friend_base)
        (person person_base)
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e1 -> (match (fst e1) T1 vX => (concat_map (lambda e2 -> (match (fst e2) T1 vY => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T2 vX vY) (and (and (snd e1) (snd e2)) (flip 0.2))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) person))) person))
        (influences (union eq_influences (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2)))
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e3 -> (match (fst e3) T1 vX => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vX) (and (snd e3) (flip 0.3))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) person))
        (stress (union eq_stress (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1)))
        (stage4 (lambda rels -> (let ((smokes (index 0 (fst rels)))
        (rule3 (concat_map (lambda e6 -> (match (fst e6) T1 vX => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vX) (snd e6)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) stress))
        (rule4 (concat_map (lambda e7 -> (match (fst e7) T2 vX vY => (concat_map (lambda e10 -> (match (fst e10) T2 a8 a9 => (if (and (constructor=? a8 vY) (constructor=? a9 vX)) (concat_map (lambda e12 -> (match (fst e12) T1 a11 => (if (constructor=? a11 vY) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vX) (and (snd e7) (and (snd e10) (snd e12)))) (Nil)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) smokes) (Nil)))) influences))) friend)))
      (Pair (Cons (union eq_smokes (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule3) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule4))) (Nil)) (Nil)))))
        (rels5 ((Y (lambda rec rels stage before -> (let (size (size_of (fst rels))) (if (or (< stage size) (not (== size before))) (rec (stage4 rels) (S stage) size) rels)))) (Pair (Cons (Nil) (Nil)) (Nil)) 0 1))
        (smokes (index 0 (fst rels5)))
        (rule5 (concat_map (lambda e13 -> (match (fst e13) T1 vX => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vX) (and (snd e13) (flip 0.4))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) smokes))
        (asthma (union eq_asthma (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule5)))
        (q14 (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_1))))
        (q15 (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_2))))
        (q16 (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_3))))
        (q17 (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_4))))
        (q18 (holds eq_asthma asthma (T1 (c_1))))
        (q19 (holds eq_asthma asthma (T1 (c_2))))
        (q20 (holds eq_asthma asthma (T1 (c_3))))
        (q21 (holds eq_asthma asthma (T1 (c_4)))))
    (Pair (holds eq_smokes smokes (T1 (c_2))) (Cons q14 (Cons q15 (Cons q16 (Cons q17 (Cons q18 (Cons q19 (Cons q20 (Cons q21 (Nil))))))))))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 0 (snd m)) (fst m))))
(query c1 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 1 (snd m)) (fst m))))
(query c2 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 2 (snd m)) (fst m))))
(query c3 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 3 (snd m)) (fst m))))
(query c4 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 4 (snd m)) (fst m))))
(query c5 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 5 (snd m)) (fst m))))
(query c6 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 6 (snd m)) (fst m))))
(query c7 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 7 (snd m)) (fst m))))

# problogex_negation.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    a_facts = get(db, "a/0", Relation())
    b_facts = get(db, "b/0", Relation())

    a = a_facts

    b = b_facts

    c = Relation()
    # c :- a, b.
    for x1 in probe(a, ())
        for x2 in probe(b, ())
            add!(c, (), x1 & x2)
        end
    end
    # c :- a, \+ b.
    for x1 in probe(a, ())
        add!(c, (), !holds(b, ()) & x1)
    end

    q1 = Relation()
    # q1 :- b, c.
    for x1 in probe(b, ())
        for x2 in probe(c, ())
            add!(q1, (), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    q2 = Relation()
    # q2 :- \+ b, c.
    for x1 in probe(c, ())
        add!(q2, (), !holds(b, ()) & x1)
    end

    queries = (holds(q1, ()), holds(q2, ()))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; problogex_tc_2.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type tuple0 (T0))
(define (eq_a a b) (True))
(define (eq_r a b) (True))
(define (eq_h a b) (True))

;; a/0: 1 facts
(define a_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.2))
  (Nil)))
;; r/0: 1 facts
(define r_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.2))
  (Nil)))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((a_base (draw_all a_facts))
        (r_base (draw_all r_facts))
        (a a_base)
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e1 -> (match (fst e1) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (snd e1) (flip 0.2))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) a))
        (r (union eq_r r_base (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1)))
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e2 -> (match (fst e2) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (snd e2) (flip 0.2))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) r))
        (h (union eq_h (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2)))
        (q3 (holds eq_a a (T0))))
    (Pair (holds eq_h h (T0)) (Cons q3 (Nil)))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 0 (snd m)) (fst m))))

# problogex_11_ads_numerical.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the

;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one

  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.

  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))

  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define edge-facts (hash-ref db "edge/2" (make-hash)))

(define edge edge-facts)

;; path/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-path path)
  (define next-path (make-hash))
  (define path-by-1 (index path 0))
  ;; path(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (add! next-path (list X Y) x1))
  ;; path(X,Y) :- edge(X,Z), Y \== Z, path(Z,Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs edge)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Z) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref path-by-1 (list Z) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ Y) x3) t4)
      (when (not (equal? Y Z))
        (add! next-path (list X Y) (&& x1 x3)))))
  (list next-path))
(define-values (path)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-path rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds path (list 1 5)))
        (distribution (holds path (list 1 6)))))
(statement (report dists))

# problogex_tc_3.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    athlet_facts = get(db, "athlet/1", Relation())
    student_facts = get(db, "student/1", Relation())

    athlet = athlet_facts

    student = student_facts

    stressed = Relation()
    # 0.5::stressed(X) :- student(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in student
        add!(stressed, (X,), x1 & flip(0.5))
    end
    # 0.2::stressed(X) :- athlet(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in athlet
        add!(stressed, (X,), x1 & flip(0.2))
    end

    queries = (holds(stressed, (1,)), holds(stressed, (2,)), holds(stressed, (3,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

# stressed/1: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
stressed_ft = [(1,)]
stressed_fp = [0.2]
stressed_c0 = 0
stressed_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in stressed_fp if p_ < 1]
stressed_fc = coins_of_(stressed_fp, stressed_c0)
# person/1: 2 facts, each a tuple and its probability
person_ft = [(1,), (2,)]
person_fp = [1.0, 1.0]
person_c0 = stressed_c0 + len(stressed_cd)
person_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in person_fp if p_ < 1]
person_fc = coins_of_(person_fp, person_c0)

person_t = person_ft
person_i = index_(person_t)

# rule 1: 0.2::stressed(X) :- person(X).
rule1_m = [((X,), (('stressed', (X,)),), [('person', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1, (X,) in enumerate(person_t)]
stressed_t = dedup_(stressed_ft + heads_('stressed', rule1_m))
stressed_i = index_(stressed_t)
rule1_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule1_m]))
rule1_c0 = person_c0 + len(person_cd)
rule1_cd = [{1: 0.2, 0: 1 - (0.2)}] * len(rule1_k)
stressed_inst = facts_(stressed_i, stressed_ft, stressed_fc) + inst_('stressed', stressed_i, rule1_m, rule1_k, rule1_c0)
stressed_of = by_tuple_(stressed_inst, len(stressed_t))

at_ = {
    'person': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(person_fc[j_], v_),
    'stressed': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp2_acc, comp2_at, comp2_end, ('stressed', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'person': person_i, 'stressed': stressed_i}
coin_d_ = stressed_cd + person_cd + rule1_cd
insts_ = {'stressed': stressed_inst}
of_ = {'stressed': stressed_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('stressed', (1,)), ('stressed', (2,))]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp2_steps = steps_({'stressed'})
comp2_at = at_of_(comp2_steps)
comp2_end = ends_(comp2_steps)
comp2_prev = prev_(comp2_steps)
comp2_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp2_steps, comp2_end, k_), comp2_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp2_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('stressed', (1,), 1), holds_('stressed', (2,), 1)]

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp2_acc = array(len(comp2_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# stressed/1: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp2_steps)):
    if comp2_ev(k_):
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)

# problogex_add.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)

    p = Relation()
    # 0.3::p(1); 0.4::p(2).
    chosen = choose(0.3, 0.4)
    add!(p, (1,), chosen[1])
    add!(p, (2,), chosen[2])

    all = Relation()
    # all :- p(1), p(2).
    for x1 in probe(p, (1,))
        for x2 in probe(p, (2,))
            add!(all, (), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    any = Relation()
    # any :- p(1).
    for x1 in probe(p, (1,))
        add!(any, (), x1)
    end
    # any :- p(2).
    for x1 in probe(p, (2,))
        add!(any, (), x1)
    end

    none = Relation()
    # none :- \+ p(1), \+ p(2).
    add!(none, (), !holds(p, (1,)) & !holds(p, (2,)))

    queries = (holds(p, (1,)), holds(p, (2,)), holds(all, ()), holds(none, ()), holds(any, ()))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; problogex_add.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type sym (c_1) (c_2))
(define-type tuple0 (T0))
(define-type tuple1 (T1 a1))
(define (eq_p a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_all a b) (True))
(define (eq_none a b) (True))
(define (eq_any a b) (True))


;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((rule5 (let (k1 (if (flip 0.3) 0 (if (flip 0.5714285714285715) 1 2))) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_1)) (and (True) (== k1 0))) (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_2)) (and (True) (== k1 1))) (Nil))) (Nil))))
        (p (union eq_p (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule5) (map (lambda x -> (index 1 x)) rule5))))
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e3 -> (match (fst e3) T1 a2 => (if (constructor=? a2 (c_1)) (concat_map (lambda e5 -> (match (fst e5) T1 a4 => (if (constructor=? a4 (c_2)) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (snd e3) (snd e5))) (Nil)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) p) (Nil)))) p))
        (all (union eq_all (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1)))
        (rule3 (concat_map (lambda e7 -> (match (fst e7) T1 a6 => (if (constructor=? a6 (c_1)) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (snd e7)) (Nil)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) p))
        (rule4 (concat_map (lambda e9 -> (match (fst e9) T1 a8 => (if (constructor=? a8 (c_2)) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (snd e9)) (Nil)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) p))
        (any (union eq_any (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule3) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule4))))
        (rule2 (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (not (any_holds (lambda t11 -> (match t11 T1 a10 => (constructor=? a10 (c_1)))) p)) (not (any_holds (lambda t13 -> (match t13 T1 a12 => (constructor=? a12 (c_2)))) p)))) (Nil)) (Nil)))
        (none (union eq_none (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2)))
        (q14 (holds eq_p p (T1 (c_1))))
        (q15 (holds eq_p p (T1 (c_2))))
        (q16 (holds eq_all all (T0)))
        (q17 (holds eq_none none (T0)))
        (q18 (holds eq_any any (T0))))
    (Pair (True) (Cons q14 (Cons q15 (Cons q16 (Cons q17 (Cons q18 (Nil)))))))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 0 (snd m)))))
(query c1 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 1 (snd m)))))
(query c2 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 2 (snd m)))))
(query c3 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 3 (snd m)))))
(query c4 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 4 (snd m)))))

:- pita.
:- begin_lpad.
:- table smokes/1.
stress(X):0.3 :- person(X).
influences(X,Y):0.2 :- person(X), person(Y).
smokes(X) :- stress(X).
smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
asthma(X) <- smokes(X):0.4.
person(1).
person(2).
person(3).
person(4).
friend(1,2).
friend(2,1).
friend(2,4).
friend(3,2).
friend(4,2).

    forall((Q = smokes(1), prob(Q, (smokes(2), \+ (influences(4,2))), P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = smokes(2), prob(Q, (smokes(2), \+ (influences(4,2))), P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = smokes(3), prob(Q, (smokes(2), \+ (influences(4,2))), P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = smokes(4), prob(Q, (smokes(2), \+ (influences(4,2))), P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),

    forall((Q = asthma(3), prob(Q, (smokes(2), \+ (influences(4,2))), P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),

# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from

# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),

# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does

    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest

    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end

end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    edge_facts = get(db, "edge/2", Relation())

    edge = edge_facts

    # path/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    path = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(path) || length(path) != before
        before = length(path)
        path_by_1 = index(path, 1)
        next_path = Relation()
        # path(X,Y) :- edge(X,Y).
        for ((X, Y), x1) in edge
            add!(next_path, (X, Y), x1)
        end
        # path(X,Y) :- edge(X,Z), Y \== Z, path(Z,Y).
        for ((X, Z), x1) in edge
            for ((_, Y), x2) in get(path_by_1, (Z,), NONE)
                Y !== Z || continue
                add!(next_path, (X, Y), x1 & x2)
            end
        end
        path = next_path
        stage += 1
    end

    queries = (holds(path, (1, 5)), holds(path, (1, 6)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    position_facts = get(db, "position/1", Relation())

    position = position_facts

    card = Relation()
    # 0.25::card(C,q,h); 0.25::card(C,k,h); 0.25::card(C,q,s); 0.25::card(C,k,s) :- position(C).
    for ((C,), x1) in position
        chosen = choose(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25)
        add!(card, (C, :q, :h), x1 & chosen[1])
        add!(card, (C, :k, :h), x1 & chosen[2])
        add!(card, (C, :q, :s), x1 & chosen[3])
        add!(card, (C, :k, :s), x1 & chosen[4])
    end

    card_by_2_3 = index(card, 2, 3)
    doublecard = Relation()
    # doublecard :- card(C1,X,Y), card(C2,X,Y), C1 < C2.
    for ((C1, X, Y), x1) in card
        for ((C2, _, _), x2) in get(card_by_2_3, (X, Y), NONE)
            C1 < C2 || continue
            add!(doublecard, (), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    card_by_1 = index(card, 1)
    samecard = Relation()
    # samecard(A,B) :- card(1,A,B), card(2,A,B).
    for ((_, A, B), x1) in get(card_by_1, (1,), NONE)
        for x2 in probe(card, (2, A, B))
            add!(samecard, (A, B), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(doublecard, ()), holds(samecard, (:q, :h)), holds(samecard, (:q, :s)), holds(samecard, (:k, :h)), holds(samecard, (:k, :s)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; problogex_advars_smokers.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define person-facts (hash-ref db "person/1" (make-hash)))
(define friend-facts (hash-ref db "friend/2" (make-hash)))

(define friend friend-facts)

(define person person-facts)

(define influences (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.2::influences(X,Y) :- person(X), person(Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs person)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-hash-pairs person)])
      (match-define (cons (list Y) x3) t4)
      (add! influences (list X Y) (&& x1 x3 (flip 0.2))))))

(define stress (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.3::stress(X) :- person(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs person)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! stress (list X) (&& x1 (flip 0.3)))))

;; smokes/1: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-smokes smokes)
  (define next-smokes (make-hash))
  ;; smokes(X) :- stress(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs stress)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! next-smokes (list X) x1))
  ;; smokes(X) :- friend(X,Y), influences(Y,X), smokes(Y).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs friend)])
    (match-define (cons (list X Y) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe influences (list Y X)))])
      (for ([x4 (in-list (probe smokes (list Y)))])
        (add! next-smokes (list X) (&& x1 x3 x4)))))
  (list next-smokes))
(define-values (smokes)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-smokes rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define asthma (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.4::asthma(X) :- smokes(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs smokes)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (add! asthma (list X) (&& x1 (flip 0.4)))))

(statement (observe! (holds smokes (list 2))))
(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds smokes (list 1)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 2)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 3)))
        (distribution (holds smokes (list 4)))
        (distribution (holds asthma (list 1)))
        (distribution (holds asthma (list 2)))
        (distribution (holds asthma (list 3)))
        (distribution (holds asthma (list 4)))))
(statement (report dists))

% ProbLog's example 9_packing_problem (test/9_packing_problem.pl)
%System test 9 - the packing problem
%Description: We want to pack our bag for a trip, but we cannot exceed some limmits. We want to know whether we may exceed the weight limit at the airport and with what probability.
%Query: what is the probability that we pack number of objects which exceed the weight limit (weight of 6) for our bag.
%Expected outcome:  
% excess(8) 0.11805555555555566

weight(skis,6).
weight(boots,4).
weight(helmet,3).
weight(gloves,2).

% intensional probabilistic fact with flexible probability:
P::pack(Item) :- weight(Item,Weight),  P is 1.0/Weight.

excess(Limit) :- excess([skis,boots,helmet,gloves],Limit). % all possible items
excess([],Limit) :- Limit<0.
excess([I|R],Limit) :- pack(I), weight(I,W), L is Limit-W, excess(R,L).
excess([I|R],Limit) :- \+pack(I), excess(R,Limit).


%%% Queries
query(excess(8)).

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; problogex_negation.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define a-facts (hash-ref db "a/0" (make-hash)))
(define b-facts (hash-ref db "b/0" (make-hash)))

(define a a-facts)

(define b b-facts)

(define c (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; c :- a, b.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe a (list)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe b (list)))])
      (add! c (list) (&& x1 x2))))
  ;; c :- a, \+ b.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe a (list)))])
    (add! c (list) (&& (! (holds b (list))) x1))))

(define q1 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q1 :- b, c.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe b (list)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe c (list)))])
      (add! q1 (list) (&& x1 x2)))))

(define q2 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q2 :- \+ b, c.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe c (list)))])
    (add! q2 (list) (&& (! (holds b (list))) x1))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds q1 (list)))
        (distribution (holds q2 (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

# problogex_coin.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    heads1_facts = get(db, "heads1/0", Relation())
    heads2_facts = get(db, "heads2/0", Relation())

    heads1 = heads1_facts

    heads2 = heads2_facts

    someHeads = Relation()
    # someHeads :- heads1.
    for x1 in probe(heads1, ())
        add!(someHeads, (), x1)
    end
    # someHeads :- heads2.
    for x1 in probe(heads2, ())
        add!(someHeads, (), x1)
    end

    twoHeads = Relation()
    # twoHeads :- heads1, heads2.
    for x1 in probe(heads1, ())
        for x2 in probe(heads2, ())
            add!(twoHeads, (), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(someHeads, ()), holds(twoHeads, ()))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end
